features.name: id_minmax_position
features.description: Scales row id to the unit interval using training-fold minimum and maximum, then clips values outside the observed span.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a smooth corpus-index coordinate that a linear SVM can weight without relying on raw magnitude.

features.name: id_log_position
features.description: Log-scales row id by the training-fold maximum to compress large index differences while preserving ordering.
features.expected_model_benefit: Adds a monotone nonlinear projection useful when corpus drift is stronger at smaller index values.

features.name: id_edge_distance_score
features.description: Measures closeness of id to either end of the observed id range; 0 is near the midpoint and 1 is near an edge.
features.expected_model_benefit: Gives a linear margin access to a simple U-shaped corpus-position effect.

features.name: project_qemu_centered
features.description: Frequency-centered indicator for project identity: qemu gets 1 minus its training-fold share, FFmpeg gets the negative of that share, and unknown projects get 0.
features.expected_model_benefit: Represents project membership as a centered coordinate, improving compatibility with linear margins.

features.name: commit_top_frequency_score
features.description: Assigns fold-observed frequency to the most recurrent commit identifiers from metadata and a small fallback to others.
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures repeated patch-batch structure as a smooth low-cardinality coordinate while avoiding direct memorization of every commit.

features.name: id_project_interaction
features.description: Product of clipped standardized id and the centered project coordinate, using training-fold metadata constants.
features.expected_model_benefit: Precomputes a project-specific corpus-position projection that a linear SVM cannot form from separate coordinates alone.

features.name: control_flow_complexity_score
features.description: Assesses nesting, branching, loops, goto paths, early returns, and state-machine style flow in func. 0 means simple straight-line code; 1 means highly branched or stateful code.
features.expected_model_benefit: Adds a smooth complexity axis that can shift the margin for functions whose logic is hard to audit.

features.name: memory_access_intensity_score
features.description: Assesses pointer dereferences, array indexing, casts, buffer operations, raw address arithmetic, and manual memory layout in func. 0 means little direct memory manipulation; 1 means dense low-level memory manipulation.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a direct continuous signal for raw memory usage that token-level patterns may scatter across many terms.

features.name: input_validation_gap_score
features.description: Assesses whether sizes, indices, enum values, pointers, return values, and external inputs are checked before risky use. 0 means checks are systematic and near each use; 1 means checks are missing, distant, or incomplete.
features.expected_model_benefit: Separates risky-use patterns along a single near-linear direction: unchecked inputs versus nearby guards.

features.name: numeric_boundary_risk_score
features.description: Assesses potential for overflow, underflow, shift-width issues, signed or unsigned surprises, truncation, scaling, and length calculation mistakes. 0 means arithmetic is simple and bounded; 1 means boundary behavior is hard to verify.
features.expected_model_benefit: Highlights arithmetic boundary patterns that are not captured by project or commit metadata.

features.name: resource_cleanup_fragility_score
features.description: Assesses consistency of allocation, free, refcount, descriptor, lock, JNI local-ref, error path, and cleanup handling. 0 means coherent and complete cleanup; 1 means fragile, inconsistent, or unclear cleanup.
features.expected_model_benefit: Gives the margin a coherent cleanup-quality dimension across different APIs and coding styles.

features.name: external_interface_exposure_score
features.description: Assesses interaction with parsers, files, sockets, devices, hypervisors, JNI, DMA, or other trust-boundary APIs. 0 means internal helper only; 1 means exposed to complex outside-controlled data or privileged interfaces.
features.expected_model_benefit: Adds an exposure axis for code near parsers, devices, sockets, JNI, or hypervisor boundaries.
